published_prior_art.cite: LiMaoPearl2022 studies finite-sample-size requirements for specified probability-of-causation intervals; Huwang1995 and McGrathBurke2024 study rare-binomial interval calibration, not this directional four-cell profile experiment.

TianWu2025 gives regular semiparametric PN inference; CuellarKennedy2020 gives regular influence-function inference for a projection of probability of causation, neither giving the stated shrinking-factual-probability shell.
TianWu2025 gives regular PS inference under monotonicity; no verified cited work gives the separate rare-PS shell and m1-learning rate.
GleserHwang1987 supplies a general expected-diameter impossibility mechanism; the bounded monotone PN/PS two-point reduction is not stated there.
TianWu2025 is regular PN/PS inference and MikushevaSun2022 is many-weak linear-IV AR inversion; neither gives a rare directional finite-profile-to-continuous-law coupling.
HannartNaveau2018 and KirilioukNaveau2020 optimize climate-event evidence, but do not establish selection-honest learned-score profile-LR inversion.

novelty_flags.label: PN/PS rare-scale score and lower-frontier claims
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey misses the close regular probability-of-causation inference comparators CuellarKennedy2020 and the public theorem-text preprint ZhangWangMiao2025; both must be positioned against the rare monotone point-identified shell.

novelty_flags.label: thm:finite-experiment and thm:lower
novelty_flags.one_line: Their consumers are generic—"finite-support PN and PS analyses with valid rare-count calibration" and "It distinguishes finite information from interval-construction failure"—without a named paper, applied domain, or open problem.

soundness_flags.label: thm:finite-experiment
soundness_flags.one_line: def:finite-profiles never defines the least-favorable randomized upper-tail p-value or its least-favorable law, so the reported confidence set is not a uniquely specified statistic whose exact coverage can be assessed.

soundness_flags.label: thm:score-pn and thm:score-ps
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed infima and suprema range over M^PN(d) and M^PS(d), but those classes omit the score-information and rare-moment restrictions; define Gaussian sub-shells and state both upper and lower frontier claims on the same domain.

soundness_flags.label: thm:score-pn and thm:score-ps
soundness_flags.one_line: Relative consistency of the named empirical score variances is load-bearing but is neither an enumerated assumption nor derived from the stated primitive learning and rare-score conditions.

soundness_flags.label: ass:pn-rare-score-moment and ass:ps-rare-score-moment
soundness_flags.one_line: With binary Y, fixed overlap, t in [0,1], and the score-information upper bound, each score is uniformly bounded and its (2+delta)-moment bound follows from its O(d) second moment; retain it only if weakening overlap or boundedness.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:continuous-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: T2 invokes a continuous LR distribution, Lambda^cont,d, and C^cont,d without constructing the continuous profile-LR statistic or its null calibration; the pilot route must define that target before approximation can be posed.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Finite marked-Poisson conclusion
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The marked-Poisson LR limit is conditional on the explicitly stated rare-mark intensity, mark-measure, and common-cell likelihood-remainder conditions.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Finite positive-denominator randomized coverage is unconditional within the abstract finite experiment; its marked-Poisson boundary conclusion is only under def:marked-poisson.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define the randomized least-favorable p-value explicitly, including the supremum over null profiles, tail randomization, and measurability convention; then state finite coverage for that exact set.

Replace the current directional shells by score-regular Gaussian sub-shells, prove relative empirical-variance consistency from primitive conditions, and restrict the least-favorable lower proof to the identical shell.

Add Cuellar and Kennedy (2020) and Zhang, Wang, and Miao (2025) to related work, stating precisely why their regular/projection or partial-ID results do not subsume the rare monotone point-identified frontier.

recommended_next_step: Revise the profile statistic and common Gaussian-shell domain, derive rather than assume variance consistency, and repair the missing closest-comparator survey before advancing.
